feedback: If the learner names only advantages, the panel presses for the conditions under which the design fails.
If the learner justifies on appearance or size, redirect to how the feature counters the hazard mechanism and what the test data showed.
Strongest when run after the learner has collected test data to cite.
activities.intendedInsight: Evaluating a design means defending its merit with evidence and conceding its limits, not asserting that one option is simply 'better'.
learnerActions: Present a chosen solution, citing the test-bench data on how much protection it provides and at what cost.
Respond to probing questions in role: 'What happens in a bigger storm?' 'Is it worth the cost?' 'Would it protect against a different hazard?'
Justify a merit claim by weighing advantages against limitations, naming at least one genuine failure point.
activities.title: Defend your design to a sceptical engineering/community panel

feedback: If the mechanism is missing, ask 'what is this part doing to the water or wind, and why does that help?'
If a learner uses one solution for every hazard, have them identify the hazard's mechanism first, then the matching feature.
activities.intendedInsight: A feature works by countering a specific damage mechanism; whether a design helps depends on matching that mechanism and having enough capacity for the hazard's size (for example, barrier height compared with surge height), not on looks or on being big for its own sake.
learnerActions: For each protective feature, trace a causal chain from the hazard to the house: a raised floor keeps floodwater below the living space as long as the water stays lower than the floor; roof straps tie the roof to the walls so it resists wind uplift up to the strength of the straps and fixings; a sea barrier holds back floodwater up to its height, provided it does not fail first.
Match each solution to the specific hazard mechanism it counters (uplift, floodwater depth, flying debris) and flag mismatches.
Explain why a flood barrier does not help against wind, and vice versa.
activities.title: Trace the mechanism: feature to hazard
